commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Subject says Encode, but the diff reworks the Barnsley module already committed the same day in 598382330d: citations re-anchored (page-51->page-52, page-10->page-11, page-13->page-14), band table changed (0: 0.90 -> 0: 0, band 5 removed) and protected-group logic/summary rewritten; corrects existing encoded semantics and source grounding

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix encoding tested protected-group entitlement against the single-person Band 1 ceiling (barnsley_council_tax_reduction_single_band_1_upper_income_weekly, £98.05) for every household type, so a couple or family whose income fell within its own printed Band 1 ceiling (£153.92, £241.80, £329.68 on page 52) was wrongly denied the 90% protected rate and dropped to the ordinary 85%/70% ladder.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release uk-rulespec-2026-08-04 (resolver, corpus commit 029f784d): page-52 carries Appendix 3, the four-column band table, and the sentence 'These are applicants who are in receipt of certain types of disability income49, have no earnings and fall within the band 1 income from the table above.' — 'the table above' is the per-household-type table, confirming the per-category ceilings. page-51 in the same release is unrelated text (second-adult gross income disregards), so the page-51->52 / 10->11 / 13->14 moves are genuine off-by-one citation re-anchoring; taken alone those are mechanical provenance, but the module also changes meaning, so the module is fidelity. Decisive semantic change: pre-fix `barnsley_council_tax_reduction_protected_group` was an opaque external input gated on the single ceiling; post-fix it is a derived rule `receives_qualifying_disability_income and has_no_earnings and weekly_assessed_income <= band_1_upper_income_weekly_by_household_category[household_income_category]`, with two new inputs and a new indexed parameter {0: 98.05, 1: 153.92, 2: 241.80, 3: 329.68} replacing the four scalar per-type Band 1 parameters. Behaviour change is confirmed by the companion test file: barnsley_ctr_protected_couple_below_ceiling (£153.91, disability income, no earnings) now expects protected_group holds and selected_support_rate 0.9, where the pre-fix module would have treated it as unprotected Band 1 at 0.85. The other changes in the same diff are behaviour-preserving refactors: support_rate_by_income_band 0 moved from 0.90 to 0 and band 5 removed while income_band's no-discount branch moved from 5 to 0 (net rate for a no-discount household is 0 both ways), protected 90% now flows through the new selected_support_rate rule instead of the old min(rate, maximum_support_rate) in the award formula (0.90 either way), and a band_4_code parameter was introduced. maximum_support_rate stays 0.90 — only its citation/excerpt moved, so the PR's '90% max' half of the finding was already correct pre-fix. Commit has exactly one module file; PR #243 has no reviews or review comments and the commit body contains only a Co-Authored-By trailer, so the PR body is the only stated reason. No follow-up commits touch this file (git log shows only 5983823 then 2d8fded). Kind alternative considered: wrong_entity_or_scope, since the single-person threshold was applied to couples and families; I chose amount_mismatch because the entity and population were right and the wrong thing was the threshold number used for three of the four household categories.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix protected-group gate read `if barnsley_council_tax_reduction_protected_group and barnsley_council_tax_reduction_weekly_assessed_income <= barnsley_council_tax_reduction_single_band_1_upper_income_weekly: 0`, applying the Single column's £98.05 Band-1 ceiling to every household category, while the pinned page-52 provision prints four Band-1 ceilings (£98.05 / £153.92 / £241.80 / £329.68) and says protected groups are those who "have no earnings and fall within the band 1 income from the table above." The fix replaces that scalar with `barnsley_council_tax_reduction_band_1_upper_income_weekly_by_household_category[...household_income_category]`, and the companion tests added in the same commit pin the changed outcome (`barnsley_ctr_protected_couple_at_ceiling`, income 153.92 → protected holds, selected_support_rate 0.9), which the pre-fix formula would have scored 0.85. So the threshold actually applied to couples and families was numerically wrong against the printed table — the encoding read the wrong table cell — which is amount_mismatch under the stated definition ("a numeric value, rate, threshold, table cell ... was wrong versus the source"). The rest of the diff (page-51→52 / 10→11 / 13→14 re-anchoring, excerpt expansion, band-code renumbering from {0 protected, 5 no-discount} to {0 no-discount} plus the new `selected_support_rate` indirection) is provenance and semantically neutral restructuring, so this is the one meaning change and it matches the first reader's reading.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "mechanical / restructure only" — rejected: the added test `barnsley_ctr_protected_couple_at_ceiling` (category 1, income 153.92) expects protected_group holds and rate 0.9, while the pre-fix formula gates on 153.92 <= 98.05 and would yield band 1 → 0.85; the meaning genuinely changed for 3 of 4 household categories. (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage" — rejected: all four Band-1 ceilings were already encoded pre-fix as `*_band_1_upper_income_weekly` parameters with correct values, and the ordinary band ladder already indexed by household category, so the module already claimed per-household banding; the protected gate simply used the wrong one. (3) "unrepresented_clause" — the fix does newly in-line `receives_qualifying_disability_income and has_no_earnings` (pre-fix these were delegated to an imported `protected_group` input, per the deferred_outputs reason), but that is a relocation of an already-represented condition, not a missing clause. The near-miss kind a reviewer should weigh is wrong_entity_or_scope: no literal number in the file was mis-transcribed, and the mechanism is "the single-person column applied to all household types," which is a parameter-selection error. I kept amount_mismatch because the rule's entity (Household), covered population, and outputs are unchanged pre and post; only the threshold value in force varies, and the taxonomy lists "threshold" and "table cell" explicitly under amount_mismatch. Source verified through the pinned release: corpus_release uk-rulespec-2026-08-04, provision record 03a6ef4e-c68f-522b-bf11-562a3864cdc0, resolved_text_sha256 782d0352…1699c3. Band-code renumbering check: pre band 5 → rate 0 and post band 0 → rate 0 are equivalent, and pre `min(rate, maximum_support_rate)` equals post `selected_support_rate` on both branches, so neither is a second defect.
